mechanism: The first pharyngeal arch contributes to maxillary and mandibular structures and is innervated by CN V3.
vignette: An embryo has abnormal development of the first pharyngeal arch.
lead: Which structure is most likely affected?
distractor_notes: Facial expression muscles derive from the second arch.
Stylopharyngeus derives from the third arch.
Intrinsic laryngeal muscles derive mainly from fourth and sixth arches.
Sternocleidomastoid is not a pharyngeal arch derivative.
key_expl: The first pharyngeal arch forms muscles of mastication and is associated with mandibular/maxillary structures.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Endocardial cushions contribute to atrioventricular septation and valve formation; failure of fusion produces AV septal defects.
vignette: A newborn with trisomy 21 has a complete atrioventricular septal defect.
lead: Failure of which embryologic structure most directly caused this lesion?
distractor_notes: Conotruncal ridges form outflow tract septa, not AV septa.
Neural tube forms CNS.
Ductus venosus is a fetal vessel.
Somites form axial musculoskeletal tissues.
key_expl: Endocardial cushion failure causes atrioventricular septal defects.
objective: Identify endocardial cushions as the embryologic source of AV septation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Pyruvate kinase deficiency lowers ATP production in mature RBCs, which depend entirely on glycolysis, causing membrane failure and chronic hemolysis.
vignette: A child has chronic hemolytic anemia with echinocytes and a pathogenic PKLR variant.
correct: They depend on glycolysis for ATP production
distractors: They synthesize large amounts of protein
They rely on the urea cycle
They store glycogen as their main fuel
distractor_notes: Mature RBCs lack mitochondria.
Mature RBCs have no nucleus or ribosomes for major protein synthesis.
The urea cycle occurs in liver.
RBCs use circulating glucose rather than glycogen stores.
key_expl: Without mitochondria, RBC ATP comes from glycolysis; pyruvate kinase deficiency therefore compromises membrane integrity.
objective: Explain hemolysis in pyruvate kinase deficiency.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: IgG autoantibodies bind RBCs at body temperature and promote splenic extravascular hemolysis, often producing spherocytes and a positive direct antiglobulin test.
vignette: A 42-year-old woman has fatigue, jaundice, splenomegaly, anemia, reticulocytosis, spherocytes, and a positive direct Coombs test.
distractor_notes: Hereditary spherocytosis is Coombs negative.
G6PD deficiency shows bite cells/Heinz bodies after oxidant stress.
Microangiopathic hemolysis produces schistocytes.
Iron deficiency is microcytic and nonhemolytic.
key_expl: Coombs-positive spherocytic hemolysis with splenomegaly indicates warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Inflammation increases hepcidin, reducing ferroportin-mediated iron export from enterocytes and macrophages and lowering circulating iron despite preserved or increased stores.
vignette: A patient with chronic rheumatoid inflammation has normocytic anemia, low serum iron, low TIBC, and high ferritin.
lead: Which mediator most directly causes the altered iron distribution?
distractor_notes: Erythropoietin can be relatively insufficient but does not directly trap iron.
Transferrin is the iron carrier and is often reduced in inflammation.
Haptoglobin binds free hemoglobin.
Ceruloplasmin carries copper.
key_expl: Inflammatory hepcidin causes ferroportin degradation and iron sequestration.
objective: Explain anemia of chronic inflammation through hepcidin.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Depleted iron stores limit heme synthesis, producing microcytic hypochromic erythrocytes, low ferritin, and increased TIBC.
vignette: A 38-year-old woman with heavy menstrual bleeding has fatigue, pica, microcytosis, low ferritin, and elevated TIBC.
distractor_notes: Anemia of chronic inflammation usually has high ferritin and low TIBC.
Thalassemia trait often has normal iron studies and disproportionate microcytosis.
Sideroblastic anemia often has high iron and ferritin.
B12 deficiency is macrocytic.
key_expl: Pica, microcytosis, low ferritin, and high TIBC strongly support iron deficiency.
objective: Differentiate iron deficiency from other microcytic anemias.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Vitamin K is required for gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues in factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S, enabling calcium binding and coagulation activity.
vignette: A patient on prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics develops easy bruising and prolonged PT.
distractor_notes: Proline hydroxylation is vitamin C dependent in collagen.
Serine phosphorylation is not the vitamin K-dependent coagulation step.
N-linked glycosylation is unrelated to vitamin K.
Lysine acetylation is not the defining modification.
key_expl: Vitamin K enables gamma-carboxylation of selected coagulation proteins.
objective: Identify the vitamin K-dependent coagulation modification.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is characterized by malignant Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background and often spreads contiguously between lymph node groups.
vignette: A 24-year-old man has painless cervical lymphadenopathy, night sweats, weight loss, and biopsy showing large binucleate cells with prominent nucleoli.
distractor_notes: Burkitt lymphoma shows MYC-driven starry-sky histology.
Follicular lymphoma has nodular architecture and BCL2 rearrangement.
DLBCL is a diffuse aggressive B-cell lymphoma without classic Reed-Sternberg morphology.
ALL is a leukemia of lymphoblasts.
key_expl: Reed-Sternberg cells plus B symptoms and painless lymphadenopathy are classic Hodgkin lymphoma.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: MYC translocation, commonly t(8;14), causes intense proliferative signaling in a highly aggressive B-cell lymphoma.
vignette: A child has a rapidly enlarging jaw mass. Biopsy shows a starry-sky pattern and t(8;14).
distractor_notes: BCL2 translocation is characteristic of follicular lymphoma.
RET activation causes MEN2.
TP53 loss causes Li-Fraumeni syndrome and many cancers but not the defining Burkitt translocation.
APC loss causes FAP.
key_expl: Burkitt lymphoma is driven by MYC translocation to an immunoglobulin locus.
objective: Associate Burkitt lymphoma with MYC activation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: t(14;18) juxtaposes BCL2 to the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus, causing antiapoptotic BCL2 overexpression.
vignette: A 61-year-old woman has painless generalized lymphadenopathy. Biopsy shows follicular architecture and t(14;18).
lead: Which cellular process is most directly inhibited?
distractor_notes: BCL2 primarily blocks apoptosis, not DNA replication.
Glycolysis is not the key effect of t(14;18).
Class switching uses activation-induced cytidine deaminase and CD40 signaling.
Complement activation is unrelated.
key_expl: BCL2 overexpression prolongs B-cell survival by inhibiting mitochondrial apoptosis.
objective: Connect t(14;18) follicular lymphoma with inhibited apoptosis.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Clonal proliferation of lymphoid precursors in bone marrow suppresses normal hematopoiesis and may infiltrate CNS, testes, liver, spleen, and nodes.

distractor_notes: AML is more common in adults and myeloblasts may contain Auer rods.
CML is a chronic myeloproliferative disease with mature granulocytic expansion.
ITP causes isolated thrombocytopenia.
Aplastic anemia causes hypocellular marrow without leukemic blasts.
key_expl: ALL is the most common childhood leukemia and presents with marrow failure plus lymphoblasts.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Clonal myeloid precursor proliferation with impaired differentiation causes marrow failure; myeloblasts may contain Auer rods from fused azurophilic granules.
vignette: A 67-year-old man has anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, and circulating myeloblasts with Auer rods.
distractor_notes: Plasma-cell neoplasms cause multiple myeloma.
Mature T-cell malignancies are lymphoid neoplasms.
Megakaryocyte-only disease would not explain classic AML blasts with Auer rods.
Mature erythrocytes do not proliferate.
key_expl: Auer rods identify myeloid blasts and strongly support AML.
objective: Recognize the myeloid lineage of AML.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Clonal plasma cells produce monoclonal immunoglobulin and osteoclast-activating factors, causing lytic bone lesions, anemia, renal injury, and hypercalcemia.
vignette: A 69-year-old man has back pain, anemia, creatinine elevation, hypercalcemia, and multiple punched-out skull lesions. Serum protein electrophoresis shows a monoclonal spike.
distractor_notes: Prostate cancer more often produces osteoblastic rather than punched-out lytic lesions.
Hodgkin lymphoma does not cause a monoclonal plasma-cell M spike with CRAB features.
Waldenström causes IgM hyperviscosity and usually lacks lytic bone lesions.
Iron deficiency does not cause monoclonal gammopathy or lytic lesions.
key_expl: CRAB features plus lytic lesions and monoclonal protein are classic multiple myeloma.
objective: Recognize multiple myeloma from end-organ features and monoclonal protein.
